name: Cleopas
role: Disciple who met the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus
whenBasis: The crucifixion under Pilate (AD 26–36), dated to the Passover of AD 30 or 33 by reckonings from the weekday the gospels give.
summary: One of two disciples walking to Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem, on the day of the resurrection. Jesus came and walked with them, but they did not recognise him. Cleopas asked if he was the only visitor to Jerusalem who did not know what had happened: they had hoped he was the one to redeem Israel. Jesus explained what all the Scriptures said about him. At table he broke the bread, their eyes were opened, and he vanished. They returned to Jerusalem that same hour.
body: They say to each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”

later.text: John names a Clopas whose wife Mary stood by the cross, and Hegesippus says Clopas was Joseph's brother. John Gill takes Cleopas to be that Clopas, and Alphaeus too, all one name differently pronounced; E. H. Plumptre keeps them apart, Clopas being an Aramaic name in Greek form and Cleopas a Greek one, short for Cleopatros. Theographic's data treats Cleopas and Clopas as one.

sources.title: Exposition of the Entire Bible, on Luke 24:18 and John 19:25
